title_prefix: Height-based eviction has no Core counte
mechanism: consider-peer-eviction (src/networking/peer.lisp:1565-1580) returns T for any peer that is :ready, advertised a non-negative height, and whose height is more than 1000 below ours. Its only guards are peer-state and the -1 unknown-height sentinel: peer-inbound, peer-manual, peer-conn-type and the NoBan permission are never consulted. The number it compares is peer-start-height, written in exactly one place -- the version handshake at src/networking/peer.lisp:1113 (grep over src/ and tests/ finds no other setf) -- so it is frozen for the life of the connection and a peer that has since caught up cannot escape. The drive site is src/networking/ibd.lisp:2166-2172, inside run-ibd's block-download loop, over the peer list run-ibd was given: sync-blockchain passes (node-peers node) whole (src/node/sync.lisp:60) and run-ibd only filters it to :ready (src/networking/ibd.lisp:2107-2109), so inbound peers merged by merge-inbound-peers and manual -addnode peers are in it. Core has no height-based eviction at all -- grep for nStartingHeight / m_starting_height over refs/bitcoin/src reaches only getpeerinfo stats and log lines (net_processing.cpp:1807, :3110, :3679, :3701, :3832, :5811; net_processing.h:56; net.h:208) and never a disconnect decision. Every automatic drop Core does have is restricted to outbound or block-relay connections (ConsiderEviction is gated on pto.IsOutboundOrBlockRelayConn() && state.fSyncStarted, net_processing.cpp:5292-5300; EvictExtraOutboundPeers is outbound-only, :5352+), judges the peer's CURRENT best-known chain WORK (pindexBestKnownBlock, refreshed by UpdateBlockAvailability on every inv and headers), and exempts NoBan and manual connections from punishment (:5181-5190). Our own docstring at src/networking/peer.lisp:1573 already states 'Core has no height-based eviction at all; this rule is ours'.
consequence: Executed: at our height 2000 against a peer that advertised 100, the rule returns T for an outbound full-relay peer, an INBOUND peer, a MANUAL (-addnode) peer, a block-relay peer, and an inbound peer holding the NoBan permission (granted through -whitebind); it returns NIL only for the -1 unknown-height sentinel and for a gap of exactly 1000. Driven verbatim as ibd.lisp:2166-2172 over a mixed list, the outbound, inbound and addnode peers all end :DISCONNECTED and only the caught-up peer survives. The two live consequences are the finding's. A node still in its own initial block download that connects to us inbound is disconnected on sight and will keep re-dialling -- a connect/disconnect loop we cause and cannot stop from our side, on a public node that accepts inbound. An -addnode peer that is behind is worse: connect-added-nodes redials every missing added node on each ~30 s maintenance tick (src/node/peers.lisp:1017-1020) and consider-peer-eviction drops it again on the next download cycle, so the operator's pinned peer churns indefinitely; because the drop goes through disconnect-peer and not record-misbehavior it is not even discouraged, which is what makes the loop perpetual rather than self-limiting. Scope correction to the finding: the drive site sits inside the download loop, whose guard requires a non-empty pending-blocks table (src/networking/ibd.lisp:2081-2093), so the sweep runs during catch-up and on every cycle in which a block is being fetched -- continuously during IBD, and once per newly announced block at the tip -- not literally every download cycle at a fully idle tip. That does not change the outcome for a behind peer, which is dropped within one block interval of connecting. S2: honest peers are dropped, operator-pinned peers cannot stay connected, and the churn feeds the redial loop of 33c6687d.
evidence: Worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-p2p-s2, warm image, probe file ga11-probe/p2p.lisp. (a) Guard set at our height 2000, peer start-height 100 -> (:OUTBOUND T :INBOUND T :MANUAL-ADDNODE T :INBOUND-NOBAN-WHITEBIND (:NOBAN-P T :EVICTED T) :BLOCK-RELAY T :UNKNOWN-HEIGHT NIL :GAP-1000-EXACTLY NIL :GAP-1001 T :CAUGHT-UP-BUT-STALE-VERSION T). The NoBan row is the extension beyond the finder's probe: peer-has-permission-p confirms the peer holds +perm-noban+ and it is evicted anyway. (b) Drive site verbatim over a mixed list -> (("out" :DISCONNECTED) ("in" :DISCONNECTED) ("addnode" :DISCONNECTED) ("current" :READY)). (c) Frozen input: grep for 'setf (peer-start-height' over src/ and tests/ returns nothing outside the handshake assignment at src/networking/peer.lisp:1113; src/node/sync.lisp:23-26 documents the same fact about the same slot. (d) Reachability traced by reading: src/node/sync.lisp:60 passes (node-peers node) to start-ibd; src/networking/ibd.lisp:2107-2109 filters only on :ready; src/node/init.lisp:1215 merges inbound peers into that list before the sync pass; src/node/peers.lisp:1017-1020 redials added nodes each tick. (e) Core: grep nStartingHeight/m_starting_height over refs/bitcoin/src -> reporting and logging only; ConsiderEviction read at net_processing.cpp:5292-5350, EvictExtraOutboundPeers at :5352+, the NoBan and IsManualConn exemptions at :5181-5190, CNode::IsOutboundOrBlockRelayConn at refs/bitcoin/src/net.h:771-785.
fix_shape: Delete consider-peer-eviction and its drive site (src/networking/peer.lisp:1565-1580 and src/networking/ibd.lisp:2166-2172). The duty it approximates -- dropping an outbound peer whose chain is not keeping up -- is already ported faithfully as consider-chain-sync-eviction (src/networking/ibd.lisp:2377+, Core ConsiderEviction) driven from consider-outbound-evictions on Core's 45 s EXTRA_PEER_CHECK_INTERVAL, alongside evict-extra-outbound-peers; nothing is lost by removing the height rule, and the peer set stops churning. If some backstop is still wanted it must take Core's shape on all four axes: outbound or block-relay connections only (IsOutboundOrBlockRelayConn, net.h:771-785), manual and NoBan peers exempt (net_processing.cpp:5181-5190), the decision made on the peer's CURRENT best-known chain WORK rather than on the version message's frozen nStartingHeight -- peer-best-known-block-hash already exists and is refreshed from inv and headers -- and a grace period before the first judgement, as Core gives through m_chain_sync's timeout. A regression test should assert that an inbound peer and a manual peer 5000 blocks behind stay connected, with an outbound peer that never advances its best-known chain as the positive control for whatever replaces it.
